title: Lena and the Harvest
premise: When a construction crew in the fading farm town of Hollow Creek unearths a door sealed from the inside, hospice nurse Felix Marchetti is pulled into a nightmare: the town's founding families were never buried, but harvested, and the thing beneath the field counts each resident backward toward their turn. Felix, who has spent his career dismissing the backwards-counting of the dying as a symptom, must finally believe what he hears and lead the trapped excavation crew and their families out ahead of the count. The ending demands a price: Felix stays behind to take the place of the last name on the ledger, trading his own count for theirs, and dies hearing the number finally stop at zero.
about_author: Edmund Eastwick is the pen name of a former rural hospice volunteer who spent six years listening to the last words of the dying in farm country. He now writes horror from a farmhouse he refuses to excavate beneath.

chapters.title: The Backward Count
chapters.summary: Felix, a hospice nurse, tends to Mrs. Alder, who counts down from one hundred in a voice not her own and dies exactly at zero. He logs it as terminal lucidity, refusing the pattern he's noticed across a dozen patients. POV Felix. Emotional beat: quiet dread masked by clinical detachment.

chapters.title: Groundbreaking
chapters.summary: The Voss family's excavation crew breaks ground on the old Marchetti field, and Felix's estranged brother Dane is on the crew. They hit stone at four feet—far too shallow for any foundation. POV Dane. Emotional beat: sibling friction laced with the unease of disturbing old ground.

chapters.title: The Door
chapters.summary: The crew unearths an oak door banded in iron, sealed from the inside, with tally marks scratched across its face—hundreds of them, still being added. The foreman orders it covered. Overnight, the tally grows by one. POV Dane. Emotional beat: the first hard crack in disbelief.

chapters.title: Zero at the Window
chapters.summary: A crew member's daughter begins counting backward in her sleep, starting at thirty. Felix is called to the house and recognizes the cadence from the hospice. He still explains it away—until the girl reaches ten and stops aging her words, speaking them in a dead woman's voice. POV Felix. Emotional beat: denial curdling into terror.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix searches the county archive and finds a founding-era ledger: every family in Hollow Creek listed with dates of death that haven't happened yet. The Voss crew members' names are all there. His own is not. POV Felix. Emotional beat: the horror of being unlisted—unclaimed, unbelonging.

chapters.title: Sealed Inside
chapters.summary: The door is found open. Three crew members who worked late are missing; the excavation is empty except for their boots, arranged in a row. The door is again sealed—this time from the outside, by something that wanted them kept in. POV Dane. Emotional beat: guilt and panic as the crew realizes they were pulled in.

chapters.title: What the Dying Know
chapters.summary: Felix visits a dying farmer who whispers the rules: the thing beneath counts each name down, and when a count reaches zero, the harvest takes them. Belief is the only thing that slows the count. Felix, who has never believed, feels his own disbelief like a debt. POV Felix. Emotional beat: the terrible cost of a lifetime of skepticism.

chapters.title: The Voss House
chapters.summary: Felix and Dane gather the crew's families at the fortified Voss farmhouse as the first count hits zero—the missing foreman's wife dies mid-sentence, counting. The survivors understand: everyone in town is on the ledger. POV Dane. Emotional beat: strangers bound into a makeshift family by fear.

chapters.title: Tally Marks
chapters.summary: The girl who counted first is now at seven. Felix discovers the tally marks on the door mirror the ledger—each mark a soul taken. The count accelerates when the harvest is resisted. He realizes getting the families out means the thing will hunt them instead. POV Felix. Emotional beat: strategy born of desperation.

chapters.title: The Field at Night
chapters.summary: Dane and two others attempt a night run to fetch fuel; the field itself rearranges, rows of wheat closing behind them like water. They return at dawn having lost one man and gained a memory none of them will speak of: the door, open, something patient waiting behind it. POV Dane. Emotional beat: the land itself as predator.

chapters.title: Unbelonging
chapters.summary: Felix confronts why his name is absent from the ledger: the Marchettis were the family that once fed people to the door to spare the town. His bloodline is the harvest's servant, not its crop. His belonging was always a debt. POV Felix. Emotional beat: shame and a dawning, dreadful purpose.

chapters.title: The Count Quickens
chapters.summary: Two more names reach zero in a single night. The girl at the Voss house is at four. The families fracture—some want to flee the county, some to burn the field, some to open the door and bargain. Dane holds them together by force of will. POV Dane. Emotional beat: leadership under collapse.

chapters.title: What the Door Wants
chapters.summary: Felix descends alone to the threshold and hears the harvest speak in the accumulated voices of every hospice patient he's lost. It offers a trade: one willing name, given freely, and the ledger closes. It names him—not as prey but as heir. POV Felix. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Flight
chapters.summary: Half the families flee at night in two trucks. Miles from town, the engines count backward—the fuel gauges, the radios, their own heartbeats. One truck makes the county line; the other doesn't. The harvest's reach is the ledger's reach, and the ledger doesn't end at the town border. POV Dane. Emotional beat: hope amputated.

chapters.title: Four
chapters.summary: The girl reaches four. Felix, watching her count, finally believes—not as surrender but as act of will—and the moment he does, her count slows. Belief is not weakness; it is the only lever. He begins teaching the families to believe out loud. POV Felix. Emotional beat: reversal of a lifetime's creed.

chapters.title: The Founders' Confession
chapters.summary: In the church basement the survivors find the founders' written confession: the Marchetti line was chosen to keep the count fed, generation after generation, and every Marchetti before Felix refused—and every refusal cost the town. POV Dane. Emotional beat: inherited sin made explicit.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: The girl reaches one. The survivors barricade in the farmhouse as the wheat presses against the windows and the voices count in unison from every direction. Felix makes his choice and tells no one but Dane. POV Dane. Emotional beat: the calm before the terrible bargain.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: Felix walks into the field at dawn and opens the door himself, from the outside, as his ancestors never dared. Behind it is not a monster but the harvested town—generations of the taken, still counting, still waiting for a name freely given to end the ledger. POV Felix. Emotional beat: awe and grief entwined.

chapters.title: A Name, Freely Given
chapters.summary: Felix offers himself. The harvest accepts—but the ledger demands the count be witnessed. He spends his final hours saying goodbye to Dane and the girl, teaching her to count forward instead. POV Felix. Emotional beat: farewell without self-pity.

chapters.title: The Harvest of Felix Marchetti
chapters.summary: Felix descends and the door seals behind him, from the inside, at last by choice. The tally marks still. The girl's count stops at zero and begins again at one—counting upward now, a life instead of a death. POV Dane, watching. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the families bury the field in concrete and leave Hollow Creek for good. The girl counts forward in her sleep. Dane carries his brother's hospice badge and takes up nursing, hearing the dying count—and sometimes, now, counting with them forward. POV Dane. Emotional beat: grief braided with continuity.

chapters.title: The Last Page of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Dane receives a package containing Felix's final hospice log, its last entry a single line: 'Zero. It stopped. Tell them it stopped.' In the field, beneath the concrete, something patient begins a new tally—but the first name it reaches for belongs to no one in the world of the living. POV Dane. Emotional beat: hard-won peace shadowed by the next harvest.
